gloss: to change (footwear/legwear); to put on different shoes

forms.label: Past polite
forms.negative: {履|は}き{替|か}えませんでした

forms.label: ている past
forms.negative: {履|は}き{替|か}えていなかった

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {履|は}き{替|か}えていませんでした

definitions.explanation: To take off one pair of shoes, slippers, pants, or other items worn on the lower body and put on a different pair. Commonly used for changing shoes when entering a building.

examples.japanese: ⟦{玄関|げんかん}→玄関：05003_genkan⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦スリッパ→スリッパ：04531_surippa⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{履|は}き{替|か}えて⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Please change into slippers at the entrance.

examples.japanese: ⟦{運動靴|うんどうぐつ}→運動靴：16864_undougutsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{履|は}き{替|か}えて⟦{体育館|たいいくかん}→体育館：03111_taiikukan⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}った→行く：00119_iku⟧。
examples.english: I changed into athletic shoes and went to the gym.

examples.japanese: ⟦{冬|ふゆ}→冬：00623_fuyu⟧⟦タイヤ→タイヤ：06330_taiya⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{履|は}き{替|か}える⟦{時期|じき}→時期：03269_jiki⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: It's time to change to winter tires.

examples.japanese: ⟦{汚|よご}れた→汚れる：01293_yogoreru⟧⟦ズボン→ズボン：01072_zubon⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{履|は}き{替|か}えて⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{出|で}かけた→出かける：00833_dekakeru⟧。
examples.english: I changed out of my dirty pants before going out.

examples.japanese: ⟦{学校|がっこう}→学校：00055_gakkou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{着|つ}いたら→着く：00680_tsuku⟧⟦まず→まず：00796_mazu⟧⟦{上履|うわば}き→上履き：10240_uwabaki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{履|は}き{替|か}えなければ⟦ならない→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: When you arrive at school, you have to change into indoor shoes first.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: ⟦{他動詞|たどうし}→他動詞：10418_tadoushi⟧ (transitive). Two patterns, distinguished by particle:
- X⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{履|は}き{替|か}える - change out of X (X is what you take off)
- X⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{履|は}き{替|か}える - change into X (X is what you put on)
The に pattern is the more common one.

ASPECT: ている gives the resulting state as often as the ongoing action — ⟦もう→もう：00602_mou⟧{履|は}き{替|か}えている normally means 'has already changed (and is now wearing them)'.

FORMS:
Compound verb: ⟦{履|は}く→履く：00700_haku⟧ (to wear on the lower body or feet) + ⟦{替|か}える→替える：13399_kaeru⟧ (to change, exchange).

USAGE:
Applies to anything worn on the lower body that is being swapped:
- ⟦{靴|くつ}→靴：00725_kutsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{履|は}き{替|か}える (to change shoes)
- ⟦スリッパ→スリッパ：04531_surippa⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{履|は}き{替|か}える (to change into slippers)
- ⟦ズボン→ズボン：01072_zubon⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{履|は}き{替|か}える (to change pants)
- ⟦タイヤ→タイヤ：06330_taiya⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{履|は}き{替|か}える (to change tires - extended usage, since a car 'wears' tires)

JAPANESE CULTURE:
Changing shoes is an important custom in Japan. At schools, workplaces, homes, and many public buildings, visitors change from outdoor shoes (⟦{外履|そとば}き→外履き：27460_sotobaki⟧) to indoor shoes ({内履|うちば}き / ⟦{上履|うわば}き→上履き：10240_uwabaki⟧).

SIMILAR COMPOUND VERBS:
- ⟦{着替|きが}える→着替える：04603_kigaeru⟧ - to change clothes (upper body or general)
- ⟦{乗|の}り{換|か}える→乗り換える：01194_norikaeru⟧ - to transfer (vehicles)
